The 2024 Pacific typhoon season was a deadly and destructive season that became the deadliest since 2013. It was a below-average season in terms of accumulated cyclone energy (ACE), but was average in the number of named storms, and typhoons, ending a four-year streak of below-average seasons that began in 2020. The season was also the fifth-latest Pacific typhoon season and the first to start that late since 2020. Moreover, this season saw an unusually active November, with the month experiencing four simultaneously active typhoons since 2019 and featuring the most retired names in a single season—nine. Additionally, the Philippines also saw multiple consecutive typhoons making direct landfalls since 2006, with some at higher intensities.
